extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates or beginning graduate students in commutative algebra / readers of algebra lecture notes
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, propositions, and key properties for localization of rings and modules, the universal mapping properties, behavior of ideals/primes under localization, and the notion of support/Spectrum in commutative algebra. Useful as a checklist of facts one may need when constructing localizations, checking flatness/exactness, or relating support and annihilators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Localization S^{-1}R (11.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define an equivalence relation on R×S by (x,s)~(y,t) if there is u∈S with xtu = ysu; denote equivalence classes x/s and write S^{-1}R for the set of classes. Addition x/s + y/t := (tx + sy)/st, multiplication x/s · y/t := xy/st. The canonical map φ_S: R → S^{-1}R is φ_S(x)=x/1, and elements of S become units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constructs the ring of fractions with respect to the multiplicative subset S. The text gives the basic well-definedness checks and notes that φ_S carries S to units; exercises following show elementary properties (e.g., S^{-1}R = 0 iff S contains a nilpotent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal Mapping Property (UMP) of localization (Theorem 11.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: S^{-1}R is the universal example of an R-algebra in which all elements of S become units: given a ring map ψ: R → R' with ψ(S)⊆R'^{×} there exists a unique ring map θ: S^{-1}R → R' with θ ∘ φ_S = ψ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UMP determines maps out of S^{-1}R and yields uniqueness; useful for constructing or recognizing localizations. The proof exhibits the explicit formula θ(x/s)=ψ(x)·ψ(s)^{-1} and checks well-definedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total quotient ring (11.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If S is the set of nonzerodivisors of R, then S^{-1}R is called the total quotient ring of R; the canonical map φ_S: R → S^{-1}R is injective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When R is a domain, this recovers Frac(R). The text notes viewing R as a subring of its total quotient ring and remarks on intermediate localizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical map is iso iff S consists of units (Corollary 11.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: φ_S: R → S^{-1}R is an isomorphism ⇔ every element of S is already a unit in R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate from the UMP: if φ_S is iso its image sends S to units; conversely, if S already consists of units the identity map has the UMP and so φ_S is iso.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization at a single element (Definition 11.10 & Prop 11.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: For f∈R set S = {f^n | n≥0} and denote R_f := S^{-1}R. Proposition: R_f ≅ R[X]/⟨1 - fX⟩ via the image of X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives a concrete presentation of R_f as a quotient of a polynomial ring and is often used to reduce questions about localizations at one element to algebraic manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideal localization formula & saturation criteria (Proposition 11.12 & Definition 11.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an ideal a⊆R, a·S^{-1}R = {a/s ∈ S^{-1}R | a∈a, s∈S}. Moreover, a∩S ≠ ∅ ⇔ a·S^{-1}R = S^{-1}R ⇔ φ_S(a·S^{-1}R) = R. The saturation a_S := {x∈R | ∃s∈S with sx∈a} is defined; a_S is an ideal and Ker(φ_S) = ⟨0⟩_S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Saturation captures elements that become members of a after inverting S; these formulas are used repeatedly to relate ideals in R and S^{-1}R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of saturation and ideals under localization (Proposition 11.14, Exercises 11.15-11.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Saturation a_S contains a; (a_S)_S = a_S; a_S is an ideal. Various relations: if a⊆b then a_S⊆b_S; (a_S b_S)_S = (ab)_S, etc. Nilpotent elements satisfy nil(R)·(S^{-1}R) = nil(S^{-1}R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These structural properties are helpful for transferring finiteness/nilpotence/containment relations across localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of ideals and primes under localization (Proposition 11.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: For b an ideal of S^{-1}R, φ_S^{-1}(b) = (φ_S^{-1}(b))_S and b = (φ_S(φ_S^{-1}(b)))·S^{-1}R. For a an ideal of R, φ_S(a)·S^{-1}R = a_S. If p is prime with p∩S=∅ then p = φ_S^{-1}(p·S^{-1}R) and p·S^{-1}R is prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives explicit correspondences for ideals and primes; in particular primeness is preserved when the prime avoids S, and the inverse and extension operations are controlled by saturation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bijection between saturated ideals/primes and ideals/primes of S^{-1}R (Corollary 11.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: The map a ↦ a·S^{-1}R is an inclusion-preserving bijection between ideals a of R with a = a_S and ideals of S^{-1}R; similarly p ↦ p·S^{-1}R gives a bijection between primes of R with p∩S=∅ and primes of S^{-1}R (inverse: contraction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to move ideal-theoretic questions back and forth; 'saturated' is the necessary condition for bijectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization at a prime and local property (Definition 11.19 & Proposition 11.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a prime p set S = R  ackslash p and R_p := S^{-1}R. Then R_p is a local ring whose maximal ideal is p·R_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constructs the canonical local ring associated to p and characterizes units/nonunits: an element x/s is a unit iff x∉p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intermediate localizations and composition rule (Propositions 11.26 & Corollary 11.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: If T' is a multiplicative subset of S^{-1}R with preimage T⊆R and S⊆T, then (T')(1)(S^{-1}R) = T^{-1}R. In particular, if p⊆q are primes then R_p is the localization of R_q at p·R_q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These facts let you iterate localizations and identify localizations of localizations with single-step localizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization commutes with polynomial extension (Proposition 11.29 & Corollary 11.30)
rubrics_metrics.description: (S^{-1}R)[X] ≅ S^{-1}(R[X]). Consequently, for p⊂R[X], p prime and p∩S=∅, p is prime in R[X] iff p·(S^{-1}R)[X] is prime and p = contraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when studying primes in polynomial rings after inverting elements; the corollary discusses prime extension/contraction for polynomial rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization preserves normality for domains (Exercise 11.31)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is a domain and normal, then S^{-1}R is normal for any multiplicative S with 0∉S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an exercise in the text; it is an important permanence property for integral closure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of module localizability (Proposition 12.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: An R-module M admits a compatible S^{-1}R-module structure iff for all s∈S the multiplication map s: M → M is bijective; when this holds the S^{-1}R-structure is unique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a necessary and sufficient condition for an R-module to 'already be' local with respect to S; foundational for module localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Localization of a module S^{-1}M (12.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define an equivalence on M×S by (m,s)~(n,t) if ∃u∈S with utm = usn; denote classes m/s and set S^{-1}M with R-action (a/s)·(m/t) = am/st. The canonical map φ_S: M → S^{-1}M is m ↦ m/1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction mirrors ring localization; examples include Mf for S={f^n} and Mp for S=R ackslash p. The section records basic identities (e.g., S^{-1}(aM)=a·S^{-1}M).

rubrics_metrics.name: UMP for module localization (Theorem 12.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: S^{-1}M is the universal S^{-1}R-module equipped with an R-linear map from M: any R-linear map M→N where N is an S^{-1}R-module factors uniquely through S^{-1}M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the universal property for module localization; used to define induced maps and functoriality (12.8).

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization as left adjoint and preservation of colimits (Theorem 12.9 & Corollary 12.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: The functor M ↦ S^{-1}M is left adjoint to restriction of scalars, hence it preserves direct limits (equivalently direct sums and cokernels).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains many exactness and finiteness-preservation properties; used in Watts' theorem arguments to identify S^{-1}(-) with tensoring by S^{-1}R.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization is exact (Theorem 12.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: The functor S^{-1}(-) is exact: it preserves kernels and cokernels, so short exact sequences remain exact after localizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two proofs are given: via preservation of injectives and cokernels and via filtered colimit argument. Consequences include that S^{-1}R is flat over R and many local arguments reduce to localizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: S^{-1}R is flat over R (Corollary 12.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: As localization is exact, S^{-1}R is flat as an R-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flatness is central: it ensures tensoring with S^{-1}R remains exact; Corollary used in many subsequent propositions (e.g., relating Hom and localization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finiteness and base change results (Proposition 12.20 & 12.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is finitely generated and elements m_i generate S^{-1}M, then after inverting some f∈S the m_i generate M_f over R_f. If M finitely presented and S^{-1}M is free of rank n, then after inverting h∈S the localized module M_h is free of rank n. There is a canonical map S^{-1}Hom_R(M,N) → Hom_{S^{-1}R}(S^{-1}M,S^{-1}N) which is injective if M is finitely generated and an iso if M is finitely presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These transfer finiteness and Hom-properties through localization and are standard 'pass to a localization' lemmas used in algebraic geometry and commutative algebra proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Spec(R), Zariski topology, principal opens (13.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spec(R) is the set of prime ideals. For an ideal a let V(a) = {p ∈ Spec(R) | a ⊆ p} be closed sets; principal open sets D(f) := Spec(R) ackslash V(f) form a basis. A ring map φ: R→R' induces Spec(φ): Spec(R')→Spec(R) by contraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basics of the spectrum and its topology are given, including functoriality and examples (quotients give closed embeddings, localization gives open embeddings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-compactness of Spec(R) (Proposition 13.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spec(R) is quasi-compact: any open cover by Zariski-open sets has a finite subcover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the standard algebraic argument that 1 lies in the ideal generated by finitely many 'covering' ideals; exercises characterize compact open subsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Support of a module (Definition 13.8) and basic properties (Proposition 13.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supp(M) := {p ∈ Spec(R) | M_p ≠ 0}. For 0→L→M→N→0 exact, Supp(M)=Supp(L)∪Supp(N). If M = ∑ M_i then Supp(M)=∪ Supp(M_i). Moreover Supp(M) ⊆ V(Ann(M)), with equality if M is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support links module-theoretic annihilator information with the topology of Spec; the finite-generation hypothesis is necessary for equality with V(Ann(M)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nilpotents and support relation (Definition 13.10 & Proposition 13.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: nil(M) := √Ann(M) is the set of elements nilpotent on M. For M finitely generated, nil(M) = ∩_{p∈Supp(M)} p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relates pointwise prime ideals in the support to global nilpotent behavior on a finitely generated module.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of tensor products (Proposition 13.12 & Corollary 13.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supp(M ⊗_R N) ⊆ Supp(M) ∩ Supp(N); equality holds when M and N are finitely generated. For an ideal a, Supp(M/aM) ⊆ Supp(M)  ackslash V(a), with equality if M is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These inclusions are used when analyzing the locus where tensors or quotients are nonzero; finite generation often gives equalities.
